full_text:
On the ninth day, the Ninth Wazir addressed King Azadbakht on the inevitability of destiny. Bakhtiyar stood before the throne and presented his philosophical resolution:

'Sire, men often blame destiny for the disasters that their own folly, greed, and recklessness have created!

Destiny provides the circumstances of our birth, the climate of our lands, and the turns of the seasons; but how we respond to those circumstances is the sacred trust of human character.

Two men may suffer the same shipwreck: one weeps in the mud and perishes; the other builds a raft of driftwood, navigates the stars, and discovers an empire! It was not destiny that differentiated them; it was the courage and virtue within their souls.

A noble character turns adversity into an academy of wisdom, and transforms modest bread into a feast of honor. He who cultivates justice, truth, and benevolence within himself will find that destiny aligns with his footsteps, as shown in the history of King Ibrahim and His Son.'
moral: Destiny provides the canvas of life, but our character, virtue, and choices paint the masterpiece. [ES]
